We had to balance the interests of all the participants, and we feel an absolutely uncomfortable situation if not in a situation where we are compelled to act as we act now, that we want to avoid any kind of prejudice for witness, and therefore we asked the Office of the Prosecutor to call Mr. Muharem Murselovic another time, tomorrow 9.00. But the Defence should not believe that in future we will act on this same basis, in this same way. This is only a measure to protect the interest of Mr. Murselovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I just ask, I'm not sure of the timing of flights, but it might be helpful to VWU to have a time estimate for the examination. If we're starting at 9.00, he could possibly still leave later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do not -- I do not believe my questions will be more than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be aware that we will limit the questions, question by question, on relevance. But I think you have got a concrete answer, and maybe there will be questions emanating from this line of question from your side and also from the side of the Judges. Thank you. Then in order to avoid such, let's call it, incident another time, I have to ask the Defence to prepare concrete questions for the other witnesses. I don't want to mention names. I'm not totally sure on the safe side whether they were protected or not -- number 2 and number 3 in the Prosecution's letter of 4 December. If there is intention to hear these witnesses another time in cross-examination, please produce the questions you believe to be necessary no later than 8 January 2003. And I would ask the parties to cross-check whether or not in fact all the statements or the proffers for the witnesses before us are ready. Defence Witness 015, this is related to the number -- the 65 ter number. But admittedly I haven't seen yet a proffer for Defence Witness number 15 on the list provided for us by the registry. This would be 65 ter number 26 on the Defence list. May we now proceed with Witness DE, and may I ask the usher to bring this witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may have the floor, Your Honour, just in connection with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I have the deadline. Thank you. We do expect to ask leave to question the other two individuals, and we will provide the Court with written questions on or before January 8th, 2003. My only request would be that those questions do not be tendered to the Office of the Prosecutor, as they're considered work product. And I would hate to have those questions be shared with any particular witness prior to their testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We will rule on this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First of all, good afternoon, witness. Sir, may I ask you to give your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. And only that you know that you are called Witness or Witness DE. This is not an act of non-courtesy, but it's just for your own protection on the request by the Defence. The floor is for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Ostojic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness DE. My name is John Ostojic, and along with Danilo Cirkovic, we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic. I'm going to ask you a series of questions here today, sir. In connection with the events that occurred in the spring and summer of 1992. If at any time you do not understand my question or would like me to clarify, please state so and I will attempt to do so. Fair enough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, we'd like to ask the usher to show the witness a piece of paper which has some information on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, you were given a piece of paper by the usher. Does that paper bear your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, we'd like to admit that paper as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It would be D42, correct? Admitted into evidence, D42.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour, I apologise but perhaps obviously it will be confidential, correct? Just so the record is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, if I may proceed. Can you give us your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: 2nd of January, 1986 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me just to understand. Perhaps I didn't hear you that well. Is it 1986 or 1976?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I ask, the 2nd or the 3rd of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2nd January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I was born in Gornja Ravska village, Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us generally where do you reside presently.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Currently I live in Raljas near Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what municipality does that fall -- that town fall under?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple background questions. Are you presently married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I am married. I am a father of one child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me for asking this question, sir: Can you share with us what your ethnic background is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Croat. That is my ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your wife, what is her ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Likewise, she is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And share with me, if you will, if both your parents, mother and father, are also Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, can you share with us the town in which you lived, the name of the town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I lived in Gornja Ravska, Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if we can have the usher show the witness Exhibit S1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the usher would be kind enough to place it on the ELMO so that all of us can view it together. With the Court' permission, if we can just go further back to get the complete picture, a little more. That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, I asked you where you were born, where you currently reside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where you lived in the spring and summer of 1992. Just so that I have a clear record, in what municipality did you live in in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exhibit or map that you're looking at for our purposes that's been identified as S1. Does the town in which you lived in in the spring and summer of 1992 appear on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us with the pointer that the usher will hand you where that town is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the witness is pointing to an area which is marked approximately with the letter "G. Ravska" -- I'm sorry, I can't see it. R--a-v-s-k-a, Ravska, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, you were how old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I was 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately at that time how many homes were in the town in which you lived, Gornja Ravska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Approximately 100 households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the ethnic composition, if you will, of those 100 or so households in the town in which you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: In my village, Gornja Ravska, there were five or six Serbian households, and the rest were all Croats. There were no Muslims or Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Briefly, with respect to your background, can you share with us your educational status and the highest level of education that you attained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I completed secondary education. And in the duration of three years, and I became a qualified metal worker, car body repair. And now if we can go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, I'm going to ask you some questions now relating to time specific to the spring and summer of 1992. To the best of your recollection, sir, prior to - meaning before - April 30th, 1992, did you reside in the area that you mentioned to us, namely Gornja Ravska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you share with us prior to April 30th, 1992, whether all the homes in the area or town that you lived were ever damaged, shelled, bombed, or otherwise looted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you the question from the period of April 30th, through May 22nd, 1992, do you recall if any of the homes within the village within which you resided were ever shelled, bombed, destroyed, burned, or looted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: In my village not a single house was ever shelled, bombed, or set on fire to this date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, if I may, with the Court's permission -- thank you for your answer. However, just for our purposes, I'd like to just get an answer for certain time periods. So let me ask the general question: At any time during the spring and summer of 1992, from April 30th, 1992, through September 30th, 1992, were any of the homes in the village in which you resided at that time shelled, bombed, burned, or destroyed, or otherwise looted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: During that period of time, not a single house was either set on fire, shelled, or in any way destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, just so that I'm clear, the ethnic composition of the town in which you resided was predominantly Croatian, with the exception, I think, as you've testified, four to five homes which were persons who had the Serb ethnic background, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me in the spring and summer of 1992, namely prior to April 30th of 1992, were you employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No. I went to school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Share with us, if you will, where you attended school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: In Prijedor. The secondary machine school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, it is the city of Prijedor that you attended school, correct, in the very centre city, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, in Prijedor. The name of the school is the machine energetics secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the period after April 30th, 1992, through and including the date in which the schools close for the summer session, did you continue to go to school on a regular and daily basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I attended school until the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you share with us specifically the time period that's of most interest to us, April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, whether you continued to go to school on a regular and daily basis.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I'd like S1 to be placed on the ELMO be the usher so he can perhaps share with us the route that he took to go to the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I cannot read what it says. Gornja Ravska, Ljubija, Hambarine, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your daily journey from April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, was done with which mode of transportation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: By bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Public bus transportation, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, public bus transportation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, sir, from April 30th through May 22nd, 1992, did you have classmates of ethnic backgrounds different than your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, I had classmates who were of different ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as what, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: For instance, Haris Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is Mr. Jakupovic's ethnic background, to the extent that you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Well, he's a Muslim, a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, during the period in question that we're discussing, April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, whether Bosnian Muslims continued to go to school, as you did, on a daily and regular basis, as you did, in April 30th through May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, as you sit here, sir, recollect your classmate, Mr. Jakupovic, who is a Bosniak Muslim by his ethnic background, attending school during that entire period on a daily and regular basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Share with us, if you will, whether or not you proceeded to go to school in the week or so after May 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I didn't go to school from the 22nd of May until sometime in June -- I don't remember the exact date -- due to the incident which took place in the village of Hambarine. The reason being the fact that there was no transport from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When does the school session in the Prijedor municipality typically and more specifically in 1992, when would it end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: On the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise during this period of April 30th through May 22nd, 1992, did you have an opportunity, sir -- did you -- if I can strike the question, because I think I need a foundation -- a foundational question first. If I may, Your Honour. Thank you. Let me ask you this. I apologise, Witness DE. In your school, during the period of May 30th through May 22nd, 1992, were there teachers who taught students of all three or more ethnic backgrounds, namely Serbs -- teachers who were of the Serb ethnic background, teachers were of the Croatian ethnic background, and teachers of the Bosniak Muslim ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I personally had both Serb and Bosniak teachers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me focus my question on the period of April 30th through May 22nd, 1992. Do you recall whether those teachers of Serbian and Bosniak backgrounds, whether they continued to teach on a daily basis to you and other students at that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, the spring and summer, sir, with respect to your town, was there a Catholic church or a religious institution within that town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: In my town there was a church, which actually still exists, which did not suffer any damage during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I'm clear, during the spring and summer of 1992, was this Catholic church ever bombed or shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No, it was neither bombed or shelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it ever burned or any attempts to burn or loot the Catholic church in your hometown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No. There were no such attempts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Share with us, sir, if you were ever in the military.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was in the military from the 10th of October, 1994, until the 15th of February, 1996. It was my regular military service that I did during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the spring and summer of 1992, specifically April 30th through September 30th, 1992, were you, sir, in light of the fact that you're Croatian, were you ever harassed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: During that time, I was not harassed by anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that same time period, namely April 30th through September 30th, 1992, were you ever beaten up or did anyone strike you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No. No one harmed me or beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time period, sir, were you ever humiliated or caused to have upon you any mental suffering or to be degraded in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No, I was not degraded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period, April 30th, 1992, through September 30th, 1992, had anyone at any time attempted to forcibly transfer or deport you from your hometown to any facility or institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, sir, with respect to your family, your parents, were they ever harassed, beaten, humiliated, or asked to leave their hometown during the period of April 30th through September 30th, 1992, by anyone, including people of the Serb ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: My father lived in the Republic of Slovenia, where he worked during the war. Me and my mother, we were at home, and no one ever harassed us or struck us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town in which you lived in the spring and summer of 1992, did you, sir, observe, see, or hear of anyone within your town of those 100 and so homes being beaten, humiliated, insulted, degraded, or otherwise offended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, these things happened. In June or July -- July, I think it was, five individuals were taken away from my village, from their homes, that is. They were allegedly taken to Omarska. After all these events, four left for third countries. As for the fifth one, there's no information as to his whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there remain in your town in the spring and summer of 1992 other able-bodied men of military age other than those five that you've just shared with us were taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Other residents remained at their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So other able-bodied men, were they ever harassed, humiliated, beaten, or otherwise degraded during the period of April 30th through September 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one ever touched them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to focus if we can on the day of April 30th, 1992, sir. Do you recall that date and what, if anything, significant happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: The 30th of April? 1992, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. The 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the date of May 22nd, 1992, as being an incident at the village or hamlet of Hambarine, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you share with us, sir, whether or not or what information you have in connection with this incident on May 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Well, what happened, at least the story went around - whether it's true or not, I don't know, because I was not there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would make an objection just to the value -- the relevance of testimony. If the witness is only, again, relaying hearsay as to what happened, unless he talked to someone who was there directly or -- if it's simply unspecified hearsay, I just -- my objection is relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this would be true for a line of questions previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand. Which previous lines of questions the Court is referring to, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The line of questions -- I don't think it's of relevance in this abstract way Defence counsel is asking questions to the witness, and whether or not one single witness was aware of some alleged incidents may be not of this relevance. But when it comes now down to this abstract question, as we can read it on page 63, line 1, following, in fact we have to intervene and ask for more concrete questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, I'm trying to just establish whether or not you knew and had information relating to an incident which occurred on May 22nd, 1992. I'm not asking you to share that information that you had, but whether you understood that an incident occurred on or about that date in the village of Hambarine. And then I have several questions relating to your personal observations after that, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. But it's necessary to have a break now, and then we'll continue after the break with your line of questions. The trial stands adjourned until 6.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And may I ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the meantime, I want to confirm that the Trial Chamber will sit in this case on Friday from 9.00 to 12.30 and from 14.00 to 15.30 hours. The second part will take place under Rule 15 bis because one of the Judges has already scheduled a flight and this can't be rescheduled. As regards the witness before us, I think there are no longer any relevant questions to put to this witness. When we were confronted with the admission of this witness, we took it that it would be Gornja Ravska. The Defence should be aware, and no doubt they know that Gornja Ravska and -- Donja and Gornja Ravska are no longer part of our case. It was acquitted under 98 bis. What we have as a summary of the testimony, it is exhausted and it doesn't make sense at all and it is therefore not relevant. Whether or whether or not a, at that time, 16-year-old person has some third- or fourth-hand knowledge about whether or not an incident happened in the area. So therefore, if the Defence is not able to identify additional relevant questions, this would conclude the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence does believe that the witness is relevant for a number of reasons, specifically some of the which the testimony was outlined, namely to refute the testimony by several OTP witnesses regarding the functions of schools, whether they operated, whether teachers were discharged, whether students continued to go within a critical period within the indictment. Likewise, with all due respect to my learned friend from the OTP, we did not have any intention to ask this witness to regurgitate or to repeat any hearsay items that he'd learned as a result of the Hambarine incident, the Kozarac incident, or the attack on Prijedor. However, we believe the witness continues to be an important witness, since according to his testimony, based upon my recollection, and that which is reflected in the testimony, after the attack on Hambarine, he continued to go to school. The route that this witness shared with us that he took from Gornja Ravska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We heard all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand. He can tell us from personal knowledge, information, and observations what he saw going through Ljubija, Hambarine, and then to Prijedor. I think it's important and I think it will refute issues both that go to widespread and systematic attack, the nature and extent and the severity of the purported damage that was done at Hambarine. Here is a witness who at that time continued to travel after the 22nd, and I think his insights may assist us in determining whether or not from the witnesses that the OTP called, if in fact every home was destroyed, as they suggest, every home was burned, shelled, and looted. This witness, I believe, will have testimony relevant to those factors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We already heard the witness on this. And as I stated before, it's absolutely misleading already the proffer you provided for us, and we do not accept that you continue with the line of questioning which is absolutely irrelevant for the case, because it's no longer part of the fourth amended indictment relating to Donja and Gornja Ravska. And we heard the witness and the statement -- his statement on the way to school and back from school during a certain period of time. So everything what is covered and expected by the Defence under the proffer has already been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't think it has. For example, if I may, Your Honour, I would ask him concretely, did he view the Hambarine area and the homes, since I believe he took that road through Hambarine, after May 22nd, 1992. And I believe I would follow up with the question, if it's in the affirmative: What is it that you observed during your travels after that time? We believe it goes to refute and contradict certain allegations that were put to this Court and brought before other witnesses that the OTP called. If the Court doesn't think it's relevant that -- whether there were only the homes on the street or near the street that were shelled during the incident on May 22nd, as opposed to the entire village, as the OTP has alleged, then make it clear for us. Our intent is to have him, through his travels, share with us that which he saw, not strictly within his village but in the villages in which he travelled during that time period. Also, we believe it's important that this witness will share with us the present situation, both in Hambarine and in the Prijedor municipality, because the Court has on several occasions shared with us their mandate and request to determine whether there is a continuation and revitilisation or return of persons who had left in 1995. I think this witness, having continued to live there during that entire ten-year period can share that information with the Court, if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Make I hear the submission by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, well, we don't object to those questions, but I think they've been handled -- they've been already testified to by the last witness, as far as the road. Counsel didn't make an actual proffer of what this witness would testify to, but assuming he would testify -- he travelled on the road and saw 40 or 50 houses destroyed, if that's the proffer, I don't think that's particularly relevant at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think that also the witness understands. The Defence counsel shall limit the questions to the route from his home to school but no other questions as reflected that a 16-year-old witness could testify that "there was no organised genocidal plan in Prijedor," as we can read it from the proffer. This doesn't make sense at all. So please conclude immediately your examination-in-chief on the basis and limit it to the route from home to school, and then we'll continue immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for Your Honour, if I may. I would like, with the Court's permission, to ask the witness a question for a point of clarification that was raised on page 55, lines 10 through 15 in private session, if I'm permitted to just ask him a point of clarification on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we can do it in five minutes. Please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have one slight correction for the record. On Friday we'll start at 9.30 and not 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is there a specific reason? Mr. Ostojic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DE, a couple more questions with respect to the date or incident of May 22nd, 1992. After that date, sir, after May 22nd, 1992, did you at any time while attending school or to visit the city of Prijedor pass through the village of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, I did, in June, as I had to go to my school to pick up my final certificate. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, during that time personally observe the town of Hambarine and the houses that are within that town during your journey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you share with us, if you will, what is it that you observed with respect to the homes within the town of Hambarine after May 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: I saw that some houses along the Hambarine-Prijedor road were damaged. Approximately 30 or 40 houses. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able, sir, to view and do you have a personal observation of homes that were in existence at that time in the village of Hambarine away from the actual street? Did you view those homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: Yes, I did. These houses had tiles on the roof, doors, windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection and your personal observation, were those homes that were away from the street in the town of Hambarine shelled, bombed, or burnt in any fashion; that which you could observe, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DE
utterances.text: As far as I could see from the bus, houses which were away from the road were complete, were intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May we go in to private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 7.04 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of December, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
